title: Polynomial-time conditional function
statement: Let $p$ be a Boolean-valued function on Boolean strings, and let $f,g$ be functions from Boolean strings to Boolean strings. If $x\mapsto[p(x)]$, $f$, and $g$ are polynomial-time computable, then the function that returns $f(x)$ when $p(x)$ is true and $g(x)$ otherwise is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ maps Boolean strings to Boolean values
$f,g$ map Boolean strings to Boolean strings
replaced: If a single-bit test $p$ and two string functions $f$ and $g$ are polynomial-time computable, then so is the function returning $f$ of the input when the test holds and $g$ of the input otherwise; the three budgets fit one common maximal degree.
